title: Weekend Project: I Built a Full MLOps Pipeline for a Credit Scoring Model (And You Can Too)
partialText: A small fintech startup was looking for someone to take their credit scoring model and make it production-ready. The project was more involved than I expected, but by Sunday evening, I had a working end-to-end MLOps pipeline running. This article is the tutorial I wish I had before starting.

title: I Built an AI That Autonomously Penetration Tests a Target, Then Writes Its Own SIEM Defense Rules
partialText:
Current Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS) tools just replay static scripts and generate PDFs.

VANGUARD uses an LLM ReAct loop to autonomously hack targets, adapting to what it finds and streaming its reasoning live via SSE.

After the assessment, it automatically synthesizes and deploys Elasticsearch KQL rules to catch the exact vulnerabilities it just exploited.

title: Building a Cross‑Platform Ollama Dashboard with 95% Shared Code
partialText: Ollama makes it easy to run models like Qwen, Mistral, and Gemma on consumer hardware. This tutorial shows how to build a production-ready admin dashboard for Ollama that runs on Android and Desktop with about **95%** shared Kotlin code.

title: Designing a Resilient Network Control Layer for Financially Critical Pricing Infrastructure
partialText:
• Pricing systems at scale fail not only due to logic, but due to unstable network behavior  
• DNS inconsistency, routing issues, and external blocking introduce financial risk  
• Traditional VPNs are not designed for deterministic execution in financial systems  
• We built a custom network control layer with:
  - controlled DNS for critical domains
  - segmented routing policies
  - secure server-to-server connectivity
  - resilience under network disruption  
• Network design became part of financial risk management, not just infrastructure  
• Result: more predictable execution, reduced anomalies, and safer pricing operations

title: Three Years Trying to Make AI Useful for my Actual Job, I Was Solving the Wrong Problem.
partialText: Everyone's focused on which AI model to use. The real leverage is what you feed it. I built a structured knowledge base in Obsidian, wired an agent layer into it, and then built an open source transcription app to capture the conversations that feed the whole system. The knowledge layer is the product. The AI just got useful once it had something worth reading.

title: Break the Loop: How I Finally Understood Functional Programming (Without the Math)
partialText: "Struggling to decode the 'Celtic runes' of functional programming? Stop fighting the syntax and start looking at the model. This guide breaks down FP through the lens of computation axioms, showing you that whether it's Haskell or Python, the logic of 'folds' and 'maps' remains the same. Let's break the loop and embrace recursion."

title: How I Use AI to Reply to 50+ Emails a Day Without Losing My Voice
partialText: Most advice regarding the use of AI for email processing tends to focus primarily on "speed." While this approach is indeed effective at first, the problem is that every email ends up sounding exactly the same. I used to struggle with this issue myself, but I have since found a solution.

title: The Real Ambient Scribe Question is Trust, Not Note Quality
partialText:
I built a browser-based AI medical scribe as a way to explore whether the real question isn’t just “can AI write a good note?” but “can it be done in a way that feels more private and trustworthy?” The idea was to keep everything local-first in the browser rather than relying on a backend, covering transcription, summarisation, review, and structured output in one place.

It’s not a finished or clinical product, but it clarified where the real challenges are. Privacy is only part of it, reviewing and trusting the output still takes effort, and the hardest problem is often getting that output back into real healthcare systems in a useful way.

title: Your Salary Is Growing, but Your Freedom Isn’t
partialText: A bigger paycheck does not automatically lead to more freedom. In many cases, it simply creates a more expensive routine. Once that routine becomes normal, people become dependent on the next paycheck. Financial freedom is not just about earning more, it is about creating margin.

title: Web3’s Future Won’t Be Loud — It’ll Be Useful
partialText: The next phase of Web3 will not be defined by how exciting it sounds, says Andrew Keen. Keen: The more useful Web3 gets, the less people will need to talk about Web3 at all.
